findings.location: Candidate line 5; Scope lines 23-29; Increment A lines 113-120
findings.problem: The plan names no roadmap candidate, while its stated closest candidate explicitly excludes changing who may approve a plan. Increment A may fold the existing delegated-plan approval route into a bridge route, so it is outside that candidate's boundary. This also conflicts with the project workflow requiring work to move from a roadmap candidate to a plan.
findings.suggestion: Add and name a roadmap candidate that authorizes the delegation-semantics and plan-approval decision, or constrain this plan to the existing candidate boundary. Do not retain the instruction that the roadmap is not edited if a new candidate is required.

findings.location: Increment A, steps 4-5 and Evidence lines 138-146
findings.problem: Increment A is explicitly one or two commits: the decision record is committed before acceptance, then the required spec updates are a second commit. Project policy requires each increment to be one verified, reviewed local commit, so this increment cannot be completed as planned.
findings.suggestion: Split the post-acceptance spec synchronization into its own increment with its own outcome, verification, review, and commit trailer; update B and C dependencies accordingly.

summary: The plan has two workflow-level defects: it lacks a roadmap candidate covering its plan-approval scope, and Increment A permits two commits.
